title: How Broken Bones Work
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss how broken bones work and heal. They cover common fracture types (simple, compound, impacted, comminuted, greenstick, avulsion, pathological), which bones break most and at what ages, and bone remodeling, in which osteoclasts resorb old bone and osteoblasts and chondroblasts build new bone. They walk through the three healing phases: the fracture hematoma, the soft callus (fibrocartilaginous callus, built from collagen-producing fibroblasts), and the hard bone callus that takes months. Medical intervention covers casts, splints, realignment, traction (skin and skeletal, including Bryant traction for children), and surgery with rehab. Complications include infection, pulmonary embolism from hip-fracture hematomas, and fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). Other segments include bone facts, smoking and alcohol effects on bone, a listener email from rugby player Jamie about the Chicago Sirens' Safari Sevens trip, and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and broken bone experiences
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck talk about whether they have broken bones, their injuries growing up, and the body's natural healing. They tease the show's topic and mention the sponsor.

segments.title: Bone fracture statistics and types of fractures
segments.summary: They note that men over forty-five and women after menopause are more susceptible to breaks, that the wrist is the most commonly broken bone, and that hip fractures are common in the elderly. They describe simple, compound, impacted, comminuted, greenstick, avulsion, and pathological fractures.

segments.title: Bone facts, skeleton, and bone density
segments.summary: They cover bone counts at birth and adulthood, bone density peaking around age thirty, the regeneration of about ten percent of the skeleton yearly, and the harm of alcohol and smoking to bones. They also discuss bone marrow types.

segments.title: Bone remodeling process
segments.summary: The hosts explain that bone is living tissue and that bone remodeling is a three-step process in which osteoclasts resorb old bone and osteoblasts and chondroblasts generate new bone and cartilage.

segments.title: Three phases of bone healing
segments.summary: They describe healing stages: the fracture hematoma forming a clot that stabilizes the break, soft callus made of collagen from fibroblasts, then fibrocartilaginous callus replaced by hard bone callus. The hard callus takes about three or four months, while the soft phase takes a few weeks.

segments.title: Medical treatment: casts, traction, and surgery
segments.summary: They cover setting and immobilizing fractures with casts, splints, and slings, realignment, and traction, including skin and skeletal types and Bryant traction for small children. They also discuss surgical pins and rods, rehab, and a Sawbones podcast mention.

segments.title: Complications and fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva
segments.summary: They discuss deaths from hip fractures due to pulmonary embolism, infection from compound fractures, organ damage from rib fractures, and FOP, a genetic condition where tissue trauma triggers bone growth. They mention Peachtree City resident with FOP.

segments.title: Bone myths and trivia
segments.summary: They discuss Evel Knievel's broken bones, the Bart Simpson cast episode, and a listener's story about losing fingers to a table saw. The segment is loosely tied to the topic.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Mid-episode sponsor break for a message.

segments.title: Listener mail: Chicago Sirens rugby fundraising
segments.summary: Listener Jamie writes about the Chicago Sirens women's rugby team, which was invited to the Safari Sevens tournament in Nairobi, Kenya, and needs fundraising. The hosts share the team website and newsletter sign-up information.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts invite listeners to share broken-bone stories and point to social media, email, and the website.
